question: When do eye infections caused by Chlamydia trachomatis typically show up in a newborn?

question: What is the main target of eosinophils in the body?

options.A: Free floating glucose molecules

options.D: Normal healthy skin tissue

question: What did Virginia Henderson primarily emphasize as the unique function of the nurse?

options.A: Managing hospital administrative budgets
options.B: Helping patients perform daily activities independently
options.C: Prescribing medications for minor illnesses
options.D: Diagnosing underlying medical pathology

question: Which side effect is most common with typical (first-generation) antipsychotics?

options.A: Severe gestational hypertension
options.B: Excessive production of breast milk

options.D: Extrapyramidal movement symptoms

question: What does 'validity' mean when discussing written exams?

options.A: The students finish answering all questions within the time limit

options.C: The test accurately measures what it is supposed to measure
options.D: The exam papers are printed clearly without spelling errors

explanation: Validity ensures that a clinical test assesses real midwifery capability rather than unrelated traits like writing speed. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T9#BMP312_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is the correct order of the three main phases of human implantation?

options.A: Adhesion, Apposition, Invasion
options.B: Apposition, Invasion, Adhesion
options.C: Invasion, Adhesion, Apposition
options.D: Apposition, Adhesion, Invasion

question: Why are regular follow-up clinic visits necessary for patients recovering from glomerulonephritis?

options.A: To ensure the patient continues taking daily iron supplements
options.B: To prevent the patient from catching another bacterial skin infection
options.C: To check that the patient is maintaining a high-sodium diet
options.D: To monitor for lingering kidney damage and check blood pressure

explanation: Follow-up visits allow healthcare providers to catch any signs of chronic kidney disease or persistent hypertension early. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T4#BMP216_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is another name commonly used for a hydatidiform mole in clinical practice?

options.A: Molar pregnancy
options.B: Placental abruption
options.C: Missed miscarriage
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy

question: What is the main reason for checking plasma ACTH levels after confirming high cortisol?

options.A: To evaluate how well the kidneys are filtering waste products from the bloodstream
options.B: To calculate the exact dosage of replacement corticosteroid drugs needed for surgery
options.C: To prove that the patient has been faithfully taking their prescribed oral prednisone
options.D: To determine whether the excess cortisol comes from the pituitary, adrenal, or an ectopic source

explanation: Checking ACTH helps the healthcare team figure out if the problem starts in the pituitary gland, an ectopic source, or directly inside the adrenal gland. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T8#BMP216_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which statement best describes how ancient societies viewed childbirth?

options.A: As an illness that required prolonged bed rest in a ward
options.B: As a surgical procedure requiring a team of doctors
options.C: As a natural and domestic event managed by women
options.D: As an administrative duty handled by village leaders

explanation: Childbirth took place at home and was treated as a normal part of life handled by female community members rather than a disease managed in a hospital. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h1)

question: A patient holding a slippery glass feels it start to slide and quickly tightens their grip. Which receptors sensed that sudden slip?

options.A: Ruffini endings
options.B: Merkel discs
options.C: Meissner corpuscles
options.D: Free nerve endings

explanation: Meissner corpuscles adapt quickly and are great at detecting low vibrations and objects slipping across the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which part of the fetus is typically identified during the second Leopold's maneuver?

options.A: The fundal height measurement
options.B: The pelvic floor muscle tone
options.C: The exact cervical dilatation
options.D: The fetal back and limbs

explanation: The lateral grip allows the midwife to feel the smooth, resistant curve of the fetal back and smaller moving parts like hands and feet. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why does high intake of preformed vitamin A carry a risk of birth defects while eating beta-carotene from vegetables does not?

options.A: Plant carotene cannot cross the placental barrier under any circumstance
options.B: Preformed vitamin A destroys all circulating hormones in the placenta
options.C: Beta-carotene is water-soluble and gets immediately excreted through sweat
options.D: The body strictly regulates the conversion of plant carotene into active vitamin A

explanation: The body only converts as much beta-carotene into vitamin A as it needs, preventing the toxic buildup seen with preformed retinol supplements. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h5)

question: During which phase of labor is pethidine most commonly given?

options.A: Latent phase before true labor
options.B: Immediate postpartum period
options.C: Third stage of labor
options.D: First stage of labor

explanation: Pethidine is typically administered during the active first stage of labor to help mothers manage strong contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T1#BMP213_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why does prolonged immobility on a standard mattress put a patient at risk for tissue ischemia?

options.A: Skin cells stop multiplying completely during bed rest
options.B: The patient sweats more when lying still for too long
options.C: Constant pressure cuts off capillary blood flow to the skin
options.D: Bedclothes become too heavy for the patient to lift

explanation: Weight pressing against the mattress squeezes tiny blood vessels shut, starving the local tissue of oxygen and nutrients. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is a primary data source in a maternity ward?

options.A: The national budget allocation letter
options.B: The hospital generator maintenance log
options.C: The labor and delivery register
options.D: The annual medical journal subscription

question: Why must midwives be careful when giving cephalosporins to patients with a known penicillin allergy?

options.A: Penicillin allergies automatically turn into permanent fungal infections
options.B: All beta-lactam drugs share the exact same brand name globally
options.C: Cross-reactivity can occur due to structural similarities between the drug classes
options.D: Cephalosporins neutralize penicillin molecules in the bloodstream

explanation: Because penicillins and cephalosporins have similar chemical ring structures, a patient allergic to one may sometimes react to the other. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T3#BMP124_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why are preterm infants more vulnerable to bacterial infections than full-term babies?

options.A: Their skin is thin and their immune systems have very few antibodies
options.B: Their high body temperature encourages rapid bacterial multiplication
options.C: They possess an excess of active white blood cells that overwhelm the body
options.D: Their digestive tracts produce sterile acids that destroy normal flora

explanation: Premature babies have immature immune defenses and delicate skin barriers, making it easy for bacteria to enter and cause illness. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T3#BMP220_U1_T3_h5)

question: What would happen if calcium ions could not bind to troponin inside a muscle fiber?

options.A: The thick filaments would instantly dissolve inside the sarcoplasm.
options.B: The muscle would undergo continuous spasms without stopping.
options.C: The nerve impulse would reverse direction back to the spinal cord.

question: Which Excel function calculates the arithmetic average of a column of numbers?

options.A: =COUNT()
options.B: =TOTAL()

explanation: The =AVERAGE formula in Excel automatically adds up a range of cells and divides by the total count of numbers in that range. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T5#BMP225_U4_T5_h5)

question: What main activity sets the second stage of labor apart from the first stage?

options.A: Rapid thinning of the cervix
options.B: Initial engagement of the fetal head
options.C: Active pushing and delivery of the baby
options.D: Separation and delivery of the placenta

explanation: The first stage focuses on opening the cervix, while the second stage centers on pushing the baby down and out. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do rural Nigerian midwives often need to manage animal bites and stings?

options.A: They are frequently the primary healthcare providers available in rural communities.
options.B: Government policy requires midwives to handle all veterinary emergencies.
options.C: Snakes and insects only attack pregnant women in rural areas.
options.D: Traditional healers refuse to treat any form of animal injury.

explanation: Because primary health centers are often understaffed, midwives frequently provide the first emergency care for bite and sting patients. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h1)

question: Why is studying medical parasitology important for midwives practicing in Nigeria?

options.A: Viruses and fungi are classified as parasites in local curricula
options.B: Developed nations have completely eradicated all forms of human worms
options.C: Parasitic infections heavily contribute to maternal health issues and childhood malnutrition locally
options.D: Laboratory machines require daily manual calibration by midwives

explanation: High burdens of conditions like malaria and intestinal worms directly impact vulnerable populations such as pregnant women and children in our environment. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T3#BMP116_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is the use of vacuum extractors or forceps strictly avoided for a persistent brow presentation at the pelvic brim?

options.A: The instruments will crush the delicate facial bones and cause permanent blindness

question: A patient with narrowed heart arteries does heavy work on a hot afternoon and gets severe chest pain. What most likely caused this?

options.A: A sudden decrease in their normal resting heart rate below normal levels
options.B: An immediate permanent cure of their underlying plaque buildup
options.C: A sudden increase in oxygen demand that the blocked vessel could not supply

question: What happens to the uterus between contractions in hypertonic dysfunction?

question: A midwife is transferring a laboring mother to the theatre for an emergency Caesarean section. Which piece of information is MOST critical to emphasize during the verbal handoff?

options.A: Her personal history of childhood illnesses from ten years ago
options.B: Known allergies, blood crossmatch status, and last oral intake
options.C: The exact brand of soap she used for her pre-operative bath
options.D: Her favorite food choices and preferences for postpartum visitors

explanation: Theatre staff need immediate safety facts—allergies, blood availability, and fasting status—to prevent catastrophic anesthesia complications. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T2#BMP120_U4_T2_h6)

question: What was Henri Fayol's profession before he became a well-known management theorist?

options.A: Primary school teacher

options.D: Military general

question: Which part of the fetus is delivered first immediately after decapitation is completed?

question: Name the primary reason newborn babies have a much higher risk of hospital-acquired infections compared to older children.

options.A: They spend too much time sleeping.
options.B: They drink too much formula milk.
options.C: Their body temperature changes too fast.
options.D: Their immune systems are immature and weak.

question: In a negative feedback loop, what happens when hormone levels get too high?

options.B: The controlling gland is signaled to slow down hormone production.
options.C: The liver stores the excess hormone molecules.
options.D: Target cells destroy the circulating hormone.

question: What is the primary immediate psychological need of parents upon discovering a birth defect like clubfoot?

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct effect of high maternal blood glucose on the fetus?

question: A dying patient expresses anger about her impending death and snaps at staff. What is the best initial response?

question: Why do doctors often take a small tissue sample (biopsy) during a stomach endoscopy?

question: What is the main reason for taking a gastrointestinal health history?

question: Why does pregnancy increase a woman's risk of developing deep vein thrombosis?

question: What is the main benefit of active management of the third stage compared to physiological management?

question: How do T-tubules help with muscle contraction?

question: What is the relationship between a research tool's reliability and its validity?

question: Why is a baseline urine test done during the first antenatal visit for a woman with chronic hypertension?

question: A patient with mild acid reflux needs immediate relief from a burning sensation behind the sternum. Which drug class is best suited for quick symptom reduction?

question: Who was the first person to see tiny moving organisms using simple handmade microscopes?

question: What is the primary immune structure that walls off tuberculosis bacilli in the lungs?

question: Why can diagnosing an iatrogenic reproductive tract infection sometimes be tricky?

question: Why is handling a sputum specimen considered high risk?

question: Why is 1% tetracycline ointment preferred over older agents like silver nitrate?

question: What causes blood vessel resistance to drop during early pregnancy?

question: Why do the spiral arteries clamp down tightly right before menstruation starts?

question: How does close birth spacing negatively affect older siblings in a family?

question: Which type of connective tissue forms tendons and ligaments because of its parallel collagen bundles?

question: What are the two main ways nurses and midwives share clinical information in practice?

question: Which heart valve is damaged most often in rheumatic heart disease?

question: Why must clinical specimens suspected of containing Neisseria be processed in the laboratory without delay?

question: Why do midwives give magnesium sulfate during preterm labor?

question: What part of a school-age child's growth is hurt most when they do not get proper nutrition?

question: Which computer component directly processes the instructions sent by software?

question: A primigravida arrives at the labor ward with a 2 cm dilated cervix and mild irregular contractions. What is the correct immediate action?

question: Which Clostridium species causes rigid muscle spasms and lockjaw?

question: Which of the following is an example of a well-written checklist item?
